decisions.reason: Changing delivery to a final PDF for client upload does not remove or alter the requirement that the PDF remain balanced and compatible with two-page spreads.
The existing same-message MODIFY captures Heyzine and white-label branding but omits the explicit operational decision that the client will upload the final PDF to the client's Heyzine account.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
You're welcome!

There is no extra text, only those images. I also obtained the white label for heyzine, so send me the final PDF and ill upload it to my account. Thanks

value_updates.platform_upload_responsibility: Client uploads the final PDF to the client's Heyzine account.

decisions.reason: The final-PDF delivery and client-upload decision does not change the required quality or remediation of article images.
The delivery workflow changes, but the polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style requirement remains unchanged.
Delivering a final PDF for client upload does not alter where magazine articles must be sourced.
The source decision does not modify author names, photographs, placement, sizing, or article coverage.
The advertisements must remain sharp in the final PDF; assigning the Heyzine upload to the client does not change that quality requirement.
The final-PDF delivery workflow does not change the approved Inter typeface, weight, or readability constraint.
The message's separate no-extra-text clause is already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the final-PDF delivery decision adds no further whitespace-state change.
Sending the final PDF to the client for upload does not change the table-of-contents timing or page-number accuracy requirements.
The cover must still contain correct article page numbers regardless of who uploads the final PDF to Heyzine.
The change in digital delivery and upload responsibility does not alter the magazine template, supplied layout inputs, arrangement basis, or layout action.
